idiom_name: messaging-client headers + SerializersModule or map as the token registry
implementation_notes: kotlinx.serialization is content-based by design: it writes a class discriminator (the `type` property, or whatever classDiscriminator is configured to) inside the JSON and performs polymorphic dispatch after the payload is parsed. The property-based realization therefore uses the messaging client's header section (Spring Kafka's type-info headers, or a plain record header) to pick the target type, with a SerializersModule or a plain map serving as the closed registry. Keep the class discriminator out of the payload when the header already carries the token, so there is exactly one source of truth on the wire.
code_sketch:
val readers = mapOf(
  "order-created" to OrderCreated.serializer(),
  "order-shipped" to OrderShipped.serializer(),
)
val tok = record.headers().lastHeader("content-type")?.value()?.decodeToString()
val ser = readers[tok] ?: error("unknown message type $tok")
val event = json.decodeFromString(ser, record.value().decodeToString())
pitfalls: Open polymorphism without @SerialName uses the fully qualified class name as the discriminator, which breaks on refactoring - and because it is a payload field it never helps the header path.
Serialising through a concrete type instead of the base type drops the discriminator entirely, so 'the payload is self-describing' is an unreliable assumption.
Registering a subclass in SerializersModule makes it decodable by name, so an untrusted payload field can select it unless the header is the only accepted source.
